tagline: Mac launcher with extensions, snippets, clipboard history, and AI.
verdictSummary: A personal command palette covering clipboard history, snippets, and a few AI shortcuts is a real weekend build with a cross-platform app framework. What doesn't come with it is Raycast's actual product: a genuinely native, low-latency launcher, a large extension ecosystem, and cloud sync — all real product work at the OS level.
coreLoopDIY: A global-hotkey command palette with clipboard history, text-expansion snippets, and a couple of AI-powered shortcuts that read from and write back to the clipboard.
whatYouLose: the extension ecosystem and its store
whyPeopleStillPay: A launcher lives at the OS level as a daily-use tool — latency and native polish matter enormously there, and that's real, ongoing engineering, not a checklist of features.
notes: A great example of a small utility becoming genuinely hard because of where it sits — right at the operating-system layer.
prompt:
Build a personal command palette covering the parts of a paid launcher you actually use: a global hotkey opens a centered input window. Build clipboard history that watches the system clipboard and keeps a searchable list of recent entries, selecting one pastes it. Build text-expansion snippets: a keyword expands into a saved template with placeholders like the current date or clipboard contents filled in. Add a small set of AI commands — fix grammar, summarize, translate — that send the current clipboard contents to an LLM and write the result back to the clipboard with a notification. Support custom commands as plain scripts in a folder, appearing in the palette by filename, with their output copied or shown.

Do not build an extension store, file search, or window management, and don't chase native launcher speed — this runs as a cross-platform app rather than a true OS-level utility, and that latency gap is the honest trade for building it yourself.

faq.q: Can I bring over my Raycast extensions and snippets?
faq.a: Not directly — Raycast's extensions are its own ecosystem with no export. Snippets are usually short enough to recreate by hand in this build's own config file.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: No — a global hotkey launcher is inherently a desktop concept tied to the operating system you're actively using. This isn't meant to run on a phone.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing beyond the machine you already own for the core features; the optional AI commands cost a small amount of API usage per use.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Native speed. Raycast is built to open and respond in milliseconds as an OS-level tool; this build runs as a cross-platform app, and that latency difference is genuinely noticeable on every single use.
